topic: Fluid and electrolyte imbalance with ECG changes
title: Fluid and electrolyte imbalance with ECG changes
definition: Key electrolyte disturbances and ECG features.
keyPoints: Hyperkalemia: peaked T, wide QRS, sine-wave at >7-9
Hypokalemia: flat T, U wave, ST depression
Hypocalcemia: prolonged QT, Trousseau/Chvostek
Hypercalcemia: short QT
Hypernatremia: thirst, confusion
Hyponatremia: seizures if rapid drop
pearls: Calcium gluconate first for cardiac-effect K+.
clinicalContext: CKD patient with K+ 6.8, peaked T waves.
nursingPriority: IV calcium gluconate 10 mL 10% over 5 min (stabilize myocardium), insulin+dextrose, nebulized salbutamol, plan dialysis.

title: Vagal maneuver
keyPoints: Valsalva (modified more effective), carotid sinus massage (unilateral, avoid bilateral), cold-water facial immersion
Slows AV node conduction
Contraindication carotid massage: bruit, recent stroke, MI
clinicalContext: Hemodynamically stable SVT 180/min.
nursingPriority: Attempt modified Valsalva first; if fails, adenosine 6 mg IV rapid push followed by saline flush.

title: Basic ECG interpretation
keyPoints: Paper: 1 mm = 0.04 s, 1 mm = 0.1 mV
Rate: 300/big boxes between R-R (regular); (6-s strip x 10) irregular
PR 120-200 ms; QRS <120 ms; QT <440 ms (corrected)
Axis: lead I + aVF both positive = normal
Right/left BBB pattern
STEMI: ST elevation >=1 mm in 2 contiguous limb leads or >=2 mm precordial
clinicalContext: ECG shows ST elevation V1-V4 with reciprocal depression in II III aVF.
nursingPriority: Anterior STEMI — activate cath lab, MONA-B, start aspirin 325 mg + ticagrelor 180 mg + heparin, target FMC-to-balloon <90 min.

topic: Heart sounds — rhonchi, wheezes, pleural rub, crackles
title: Heart sounds — rhonchi, wheezes, pleural rub, crackles
keyPoints: Crackles (rales): discontinuous; fine (interstitial fibrosis, early CHF), coarse (pneumonia, bronchiectasis)
Rhonchi: low-pitched rumble from secretions in large airways
Wheeze: high-pitched, continuous, expiratory; asthma/COPD
Pleural rub: leathery, not cleared by cough
Stridor: high-pitched inspiratory — upper airway obstruction
clinicalContext: COPD patient with polyphonic expiratory wheeze.
nursingPriority: Salbutamol nebulization, O2 titrated 88-92%, reassess breath sounds.

title: Pulse pressure
keyPoints: Widened (>50): aortic regurgitation, hyperthyroidism, anemia, thiamine deficiency, AV fistula
Narrow (<25): cardiac tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, severe aortic stenosis, hypovolemia
clinicalContext: BP 160/60 with collapsing pulse.
nursingPriority: Wide pulse pressure suggests aortic regurgitation — auscultate for diastolic murmur, echo, refer to cardiology.

title: Myocardial infarction and enzyme markers
definition: Acute coronary syndrome — Type 1 due to plaque rupture.
keyPoints: Troponin I/T: rises 3-6 h, peaks 18-24 h, remains 7-14 d — most sensitive and specific
CK-MB: rises 4-6 h, peaks 24 h, returns 48-72 h — reinfarction detection
Myoglobin: earliest (1-2 h) but non-specific
AST, LDH: historic
STEMI: PCI within 90 min or fibrinolysis within 30 min
pearls: No nitrates in inferior MI with RV involvement.
clinicalContext: Crushing chest pain 2 h, ECG ST elevation II III aVF, troponin positive.
nursingPriority: Inferior STEMI — aspirin 325 mg chew, clopidogrel/ticagrelor loading, heparin, morphine for pain, activate cath lab.

title: Rheumatic fever
keyPoints: Jones criteria: 2 major OR 1 major + 2 minor + evidence of recent strep
Major: migratory polyarthritis, carditis, chorea (Sydenham), erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules
Minor: fever, arthralgia, elevated ESR/CRP, prolonged PR
Treatment: benzathine penicillin G IM + NSAIDs; steroids for severe carditis
Secondary prophylaxis: BPG IM q3 wk up to 21 y or 10 y after attack
clinicalContext: 10-y-old with migratory arthritis, carditis, recent pharyngitis.
nursingPriority: Throat culture/ASO, ECG (PR prolongation), admit for benzathine penicillin IM + aspirin, start secondary prophylaxis q3 wk.

title: Varicose vein
keyPoints: Great saphenous most commonly
Risk: prolonged standing, pregnancy, family history
Complications: superficial thrombophlebitis, venous ulcer over medial malleolus, lipodermatosclerosis
CEAP classification
Treatment: graduated compression stockings, endovenous laser/radiofrequency, sclerotherapy, stripping
clinicalContext: Teacher with leg heaviness and visible bulging veins.
nursingPriority: Graduated compression stockings 20-30 mmHg, elevate legs, weight management, refer for duplex USG and consider endovenous ablation.

title: Ventricular fibrillation — defibrillation
definition: Shockable rhythm: disorganized ventricular activity — no cardiac output.
keyPoints: Defibrillation immediately: biphasic 120-200 J, monophasic 360 J
Resume CPR for 2 min immediately post-shock
Epi 1 mg IV q3-5 min after 2nd shock
Amiodarone 300 mg IV bolus after 3rd shock; 150 mg repeat
Refractory VF → consider dual sequential defibrillation
clinicalContext: Witnessed collapse, monitor shows VF.
nursingPriority: Deliver shock 200 J biphasic immediately, resume CPR 2 min, reassess, epi 1 mg after 2nd shock.

title: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG)
keyPoints: LIMA to LAD — best patency (>90% at 10 y)
Saphenous vein graft (SVG) for others
Radial artery alternative
Post-op: sternal precautions 6-8 wk, no lifting >5 kg, cough with pillow
DAPT per indication
clinicalContext: POD 2 CABG patient ready for ambulation.
nursingPriority: Sternal precautions, incentive spirometry, cough with pillow, gradual ambulation, monitor for sternal instability (clicking, pain).

title: Angina — types (variant/Prinzmetal)
keyPoints: Stable: reproducible with exertion, relieved by rest/nitrates
Unstable: new-onset, worsening pattern, rest pain
Prinzmetal (variant): vasospasm — pain at rest, often nocturnal, transient ST elevation
Treatment: CCB + nitrates for Prinzmetal; avoid non-selective beta-blockers (worsen spasm)
clinicalContext: Young man with nocturnal chest pain and transient ST elevation.
nursingPriority: Prinzmetal — diltiazem or amlodipine, isosorbide dinitrate, avoid non-selective beta-blockers, cocaine screen.

title: Bacterial endocarditis
keyPoints: Modified Duke criteria: 2 major OR 1 major + 3 minor OR 5 minor
Major: positive blood cultures (typical organism x2), evidence on echo (vegetation/abscess)
Organisms: Strep viridans (native), S aureus (IV drug users, prosthetic), enterococci
Treatment: IV antibiotics 4-6 wk guided by culture; surgery if heart failure/abscess/persistent bacteremia
clinicalContext: IVDU with fever, new murmur, Osler nodes.
nursingPriority: Draw 3 sets of blood cultures before antibiotics, echocardiogram (TEE), start vancomycin + gentamicin, cardiology/ID consult.

title: Constrictive pericarditis
keyPoints: Causes: TB (common in India), post-cardiac surgery, radiation
Kussmaul sign: JVP rises with inspiration
Pericardial knock on auscultation
CT/MRI shows thickened pericardium
Treatment: pericardiectomy
clinicalContext: Post-TB patient with elevated JVP rising on inspiration and ascites.
nursingPriority: Refer for echo/CT, diuretics for symptoms, plan pericardiectomy.

title: Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP)
definition: Mechanical circulatory support via descending aorta.
keyPoints: Inflates in diastole (coronary perfusion), deflates in systole (afterload reduction)
Indications: cardiogenic shock, unstable angina, bridge to surgery
Complications: limb ischemia, thrombocytopenia, infection, dissection
Contraindication: AR, aortic dissection
clinicalContext: Cardiogenic shock patient on IABP.
nursingPriority: Monitor distal limb pulses (ischemia), MAP, urine output, platelet count; keep knee straight; check balloon timing.

title: Cardiac tamponade
keyPoints: Beck triad: hypotension + muffled heart sounds + distended neck veins
Pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg
Echo: diastolic RV collapse, IVC plethora
Treatment: emergency pericardiocentesis (subxiphoid)
Avoid IPPV if possible (worsens)
clinicalContext: Post-MI patient with sudden hypotension, distended neck veins, muffled sounds.
nursingPriority: Urgent echo, prepare pericardiocentesis tray, IV fluids to maintain preload, call cardiology.

title: Pacemaker — types and settings
definition: Electrical stimulation of heart for bradyarrhythmias.
keyPoints: NBG code 5-letter: chamber paced/sensed/response/rate modulation/multisite
Common modes: VVI, DDD, AAI
Indications: symptomatic bradycardia, complete AV block, sick sinus
Complications: infection, lead dislodgement, pneumothorax
Patient education: avoid strong magnets, MRI-conditional devices
clinicalContext: Recent pacemaker implant patient.
nursingPriority: Avoid heavy arm movement for 4-6 wk on implant side, monitor pocket for hematoma/infection, no MRI unless MRI-conditional, carry device card.

title: Cardioversion vs defibrillation
keyPoints: Cardioversion: synchronized with R wave; for stable tachyarrhythmias with pulse (AF, SVT, VT with pulse); starting energy 50-200 J biphasic
Defibrillation: unsynchronized; pulseless VT, VF; 120-200 J biphasic
Sedation needed for cardioversion
Anticoagulate if AF >48 h prior to elective cardioversion
clinicalContext: AF with rapid ventricular response, unstable, BP 80/50.
nursingPriority: Synchronized cardioversion 120-150 J biphasic after brief sedation.

title: Defibrillator — AED
keyPoints: Deliver shock in VF/pulseless VT only
Pads: right upper sternum + left axilla; alternate anteroposterior for kids/small
Pediatric pads <8 y or <25 kg
Continue compressions while AED analyzes? No — step clear during analysis
Shave hair if needed, avoid water/metal
clinicalContext: Public cardiac arrest, bystander with AED.
nursingPriority: Turn AED on, attach pads right upper chest + left mid-axilla, let it analyze, deliver shock if advised, resume CPR immediately.

title: Cardiac monitor
keyPoints: Lead placement 3-lead: white right, black left, red chest (lower left)
5-lead: add green RL, brown chest
Lead II best for P wave
Alarm parameters: HR high/low, asystole, VF, SpO2
Troubleshoot: check electrodes, skin prep, lead contact
clinicalContext: Cardiac monitor shows flat line.
nursingPriority: Check patient first (asystole vs lead off), verify pulse, if asystole start CPR and check lead placement.

title: PCWP (pulmonary capillary wedge pressure)
definition: Reflects left atrial and LV end-diastolic pressure.
keyPoints: Normal 6-12 mmHg
Elevated: LV failure, mitral stenosis, volume overload
Low: hypovolemia
Measured via Swan-Ganz catheter
clinicalContext: Pulmonary edema patient with PCWP 28.
nursingPriority: Diuretics (furosemide), vasodilator (nitroglycerin), supplemental O2, reassess PCWP.

title: Pulmonary artery catheter
keyPoints: Normal: RAP 0-8, RV 25/0-8, PA 25/10, PCWP 6-12
Measure CO by thermodilution
Elevated PVR: pulmonary HTN
Less common now
clinicalContext: ICU shock patient needs PA catheter.
nursingPriority: Level transducer at phlebostatic axis, zero, interpret pressure tracings, watch for arrhythmia during float.

title: Thyroid eye disease
keyPoints: Proptosis, lid lag, lid retraction (Dalrymple), ophthalmoplegia
Smoking is major risk factor
Treatment: smoking cessation, selenium, IV methylprednisolone for moderate-severe, orbital decompression, teprotumumab
clinicalContext: Graves patient with progressive proptosis.
nursingPriority: Stop smoking, ophthalmology referral, lubricating eye drops, elevate head while sleeping, escalate to steroids if inflammation.

title: DKA — Kussmaul breathing
keyPoints: Triad: hyperglycemia >250, ketosis (β-hydroxybutyrate), metabolic acidosis pH <7.3 HCO3 <18
Kussmaul breathing: deep, rapid compensatory
Fluid deficit ~6 L adult
Treatment: IV NS 1-1.5 L first hour, then 0.45% NaCl 250-500 mL/h; insulin infusion 0.1 U/kg/h; K+ replacement when <5.3; glucose when BG <250
clinicalContext: T1DM with BG 520, pH 7.1, K+ 3.2, dyspnea.
nursingPriority: IV NS 1 L bolus, delay insulin until K+ replaced (first replace KCl), then insulin infusion 0.1 U/kg/h, monitor hourly glucose and K+.

title: Diabetes insipidus
keyPoints: Large-volume dilute urine (>3 L/day, SG <1.005, osmolality <300)
Water deprivation test differentiates
Central: desmopressin responds
Nephrogenic: thiazides paradoxically reduce output
Causes central: head injury, pituitary surgery
clinicalContext: Post-pituitary surgery patient with polyuria 8 L/day.
nursingPriority: Strict I/O, electrolytes (Na+), start desmopressin (dDAVP) intranasal or IV, monitor for hyponatremia as response occurs.

title: Diabetes mellitus — management
keyPoints: Diagnosis: FPG >=126, OGTT 2-h >=200, HbA1c >=6.5, random >=200 with symptoms
HbA1c target <7% (individualize)
Metformin first-line (eGFR >30)
SGLT2i + GLP1-RA for CVD/CKD
Complications: retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, atherosclerosis
clinicalContext: New T2DM HbA1c 8.5%, CKD, HFrEF.
nursingPriority: Start metformin 500 mg BD + empagliflozin 10 mg (SGLT2i for CV and renal benefit), lifestyle, statin, BP control, diabetic education.

title: Simmonds disease (panhypopituitarism)
definition: Post-partum pituitary necrosis (Sheehan) or other cause of anterior pituitary failure.
keyPoints: Loss of FSH/LH, TSH, ACTH, GH, prolactin
Lactation failure post-PPH is classic
Hypothyroid, adrenal insufficiency, hypogonadism
Treatment: hormone replacement lifelong
clinicalContext: Post-severe PPH mother cannot lactate, amenorrhea, fatigue.
nursingPriority: Measure cortisol, TSH, fT4, prolactin, FSH/LH, start hydrocortisone before levothyroxine, endocrine referral.

title: Hypoparathyroidism vs hyperparathyroidism
keyPoints: Hypo: low Ca, high P; tetany, Chvostek, Trousseau, QT prolonged; Rx: Ca + calcitriol
Hyper: high Ca, low P; bones/stones/abdominal groans/psychic moans; Rx: parathyroidectomy if symptomatic
clinicalContext: Post-thyroidectomy patient with perioral numbness, carpal spasm.
nursingPriority: Suspect hypocalcemia — check serum ionized calcium, IV calcium gluconate, start oral calcium + calcitriol, monitor long-term.

title: Graves disease
keyPoints: Diffuse goiter, ophthalmopathy, pretibial myxedema, thyroid acropachy
High fT4/T3, suppressed TSH, high TRAb
Treatment: methimazole/PTU (PTU in 1st trimester), radioiodine (avoid in pregnancy/breastfeeding), surgery
Thyroid storm: beta-blocker + PTU + iodine + hydrocortisone
clinicalContext: Pregnant 1st trimester with Graves.
nursingPriority: Use PTU 1st trimester (less teratogenic than methimazole), switch to methimazole in 2nd; monitor fT4 to keep in upper normal.

title: Iron deficiency anemia
keyPoints: Low MCV, low MCH, low ferritin, low iron, high TIBC
Causes: blood loss (GI, menstrual), poor intake, malabsorption (celiac), pregnancy
Oral iron: ferrous sulfate 200 mg TDS (65 mg elemental), take on empty stomach, with vit C
IV iron: sucrose, isomaltoside for severe/intolerance
clinicalContext: Menstruating woman Hb 8, MCV 68, ferritin 5.
nursingPriority: Start oral ferrous sulfate 200 mg TDS with vit C, investigate cause (menstrual + GI evaluation >40 y), reassess Hb in 4 wk.

title: Thalassemia
definition: Hereditary defect in α or β globin chain synthesis.
keyPoints: Beta-thal major: severe microcytic anemia, hepatosplenomegaly, skeletal changes, iron overload from transfusion
HbF and HbA2 elevated
Management: regular transfusion + iron chelation (deferasirox, deferoxamine, deferiprone)
Curative: HSCT
Prevention: carrier screening, prenatal diagnosis
clinicalContext: Beta-thal major child on monthly transfusions with ferritin 3000.
nursingPriority: Start iron chelation with deferasirox 20-30 mg/kg OD, monitor LFT, creatinine, ferritin q3 mo, eye/ear screening.

title: Leukemia — AML, ALL, CML, CLL
keyPoints: ALL: children; bone marrow blast >20% lymphoblast; good prognosis
AML: adults; Auer rods; M3 (APL) with t(15;17), PML-RARA, DIC risk
CML: Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22), BCR-ABL; imatinib
CLL: elderly; smudge cells; monoclonal B-cells; often watchful waiting
clinicalContext: Child with fatigue, lymphadenopathy, blasts 80%.
nursingPriority: Suspect ALL — refer to pediatric hem-onc, bone marrow biopsy, induction chemotherapy per BFM protocol, supportive care.

title: Sickle cell disease
keyPoints: Vaso-occlusive crisis: pain (bone, chest, abdomen), avascular necrosis of femoral head
Acute chest syndrome: hypoxia, infiltrate — mortality
Complications: stroke, priapism, splenic sequestration
Hydroxyurea reduces crises
Preventive: Hib/pneumococcal vaccines, folate
clinicalContext: Sickle cell patient with severe pain and chest infiltrate on X-ray.
nursingPriority: Acute chest syndrome — IV hydration (1.0-1.5x maintenance, not more), O2, analgesia, antibiotics (cefuroxime + macrolide), exchange transfusion if severe.

title: Lymphoma — NHL vs HL
keyPoints: HL: Reed-Sternberg cells; contiguous spread; bimodal 20s and 60s; good prognosis
NHL: heterogeneous; diffuse; more common; extranodal frequent
B symptoms: fever, night sweats, weight loss >10%
Staging: Ann Arbor I-IV
clinicalContext: Young adult with painless cervical lymphadenopathy, night sweats.
nursingPriority: Excision biopsy (not FNAC), staging CT/PET, bone marrow; refer to oncology.

title: Hodgkin lymphoma — Reed-Sternberg
keyPoints: RS: "owl-eye" binucleate cell with eosinophilic nucleolus
Subtypes: nodular sclerosis (commonest), mixed cellularity, lymphocyte-rich, lymphocyte-depleted, nodular lymphocyte-predominant
Treatment: ABVD chemotherapy (adriamycin, bleomycin, vinblastine, dacarbazine) ± radiation
clinicalContext: Biopsy showing Reed-Sternberg cells.
nursingPriority: Confirm HL, stage with PET-CT, plan ABVD chemotherapy, fertility preservation counsel.

title: Lordosis, scoliosis, kyphosis
keyPoints: Lordosis: inward lumbar curve
Kyphosis: outward thoracic (hunchback)
Scoliosis: lateral curvature + rotation; Cobb angle >10° defines
Adam forward-bend test: rib hump
Brace >25-40°; surgery >45-50°
clinicalContext: Adolescent scoliosis Cobb 30°.
nursingPriority: Bracing (Boston/Milwaukee) 23 h/day until skeletal maturity, monitor q6 mo, surgery if progression >45°.

title: Paget disease
definition: Disordered bone remodeling — increased osteoclast activity.
keyPoints: Elderly, skull/pelvis/spine
Elevated alkaline phosphatase
Bone pain, deformity, fractures, high-output heart failure, hearing loss (CN VIII compression)
Treatment: bisphosphonates (zoledronate IV)
clinicalContext: Elderly man with skull thickening, high ALP, hearing loss.
nursingPriority: Confirm with bone scan; start zoledronate 5 mg IV, ensure adequate Ca/vit D, audiology follow-up.

title: Colles fracture
definition: Distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement — fall on outstretched hand.
keyPoints: Dinner-fork deformity
Elderly osteoporotic women
X-ray confirms
Treatment: closed reduction + cast if acceptable alignment; ORIF if comminuted or severe
clinicalContext: Elderly woman with fall on outstretched hand, dinner-fork deformity.
nursingPriority: Analgesia, splint, X-ray, closed reduction under hematoma block or conscious sedation, cast, DEXA for osteoporosis.

title: Sprain vs strain
keyPoints: Sprain: ligament (joint) — e.g., ankle inversion
Strain: muscle or tendon — e.g., hamstring
Grading: 1 (mild), 2 (partial), 3 (complete tear)
RICE: rest, ice, compression, elevation
clinicalContext: Ankle inversion injury with lateral swelling.
nursingPriority: RICE, NSAIDs, weight-bearing as tolerated, functional bracing, refer if grade 3 or persistent instability.

title: Amputation
keyPoints: Indications: peripheral vascular disease (commonest), diabetes, trauma, tumor, severe infection
Levels: AKA, BKA, Syme, transmetatarsal
Phantom limb pain: gabapentin, mirror therapy
Stump care: bandaging in cone shape, prevent contractures
clinicalContext: Post-BKA day 2 patient.
nursingPriority: Prone positioning 2-3x/day to prevent hip flexion contracture, elevate stump first 24 h then avoid, bandage in figure-8 toward proximal, phantom pain education.

title: Trochanter rolls
definition: Rolled blanket/foam placed lateral to hip to prevent external rotation in bedridden patient.
keyPoints: Prevents foot drop + external rotation
Reinforce in stroke, bedridden, post-op hip replacement
Reposition q2h
clinicalContext: Bedridden stroke patient lying in bed.
nursingPriority: Place trochanter rolls lateral to hip from greater trochanter to mid-thigh to keep hip neutral, foot board to prevent drop foot, turn q2h.

title: Arthroplasty, arthrodesis, arthrotomy
keyPoints: Arthroplasty: joint replacement (THR, TKR)
Arthrodesis: surgical fusion (ankle, wrist, spine)
Arthrotomy: surgical opening of joint
Arthroscopy: minimally invasive camera exam
clinicalContext: Patient scheduled for THR.
nursingPriority: Explain arthroplasty; precautions: avoid hip flexion >90°, adduction past midline, internal rotation for 6-12 wk.

title: Gout
keyPoints: Podagra: 1st MTP painful red swollen
Elevated uric acid (not always acute)
Polarized light microscopy: negative birefringent needle crystals
Acute: NSAID, colchicine, steroid
Chronic: allopurinol/febuxostat (uric acid <6 mg/dL)
clinicalContext: Obese man with severe big toe pain, red swollen MTP joint, 3 AM onset.
nursingPriority: Acute gout — NSAID (naproxen) or colchicine, rest, ice, do NOT start allopurinol during acute attack; start urate-lowering after resolution.

title: Arterial blood gas (ABG) interpretation
keyPoints: Acidosis (<7.35): respiratory (high CO2) or metabolic (low HCO3)
Alkalosis (>7.45): respiratory (low CO2) or metabolic (high HCO3)
Compensation: partial, full, mixed
Anion gap = Na - (Cl + HCO3); 8-12 normal; >12 elevated suggests MUDPILES
nursingPriority: Metabolic acidosis (pH low, HCO3 low); anion gap 26 (high) — DKA/lactic/toxin; treat underlying, fluids; avoid bicarbonate unless pH <7.1.

title: Nephrotic syndrome
definition: Glomerular proteinuria >3.5 g/day + hypoalbuminemia + edema + hyperlipidemia.
keyPoints: Children: minimal change — steroid responsive
Adults: FSGS, membranous, diabetic
Complications: thrombosis (renal vein), infection (low IgG), hyperlipidemia
Treatment: steroids, ACE-i, diuretics, statins, anticoagulation if severe
clinicalContext: 5-y-old with periorbital edema, urine albumin 4+, low albumin.
nursingPriority: Minimal change disease likely — start prednisolone 60 mg/m2/day, salt restriction, monitor for infection, no routine renal biopsy in typical cases.

title: Chronic renal failure
definition: CKD: GFR <60 for >=3 mo or kidney damage markers.
keyPoints: Stages G1-G5 by eGFR; A1-A3 by albuminuria
Complications: anemia (EPO), hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, bone-mineral disease, uremia
Dialysis when eGFR <10-15 with symptoms
Transplant gold standard
clinicalContext: CKD-5 patient with pulmonary edema, K+ 6.5.
nursingPriority: Emergency dialysis, calcium gluconate for cardiac protection, insulin+dextrose for K+, furosemide if any residual function, O2.

title: Hemodialysis — AV fistula care
keyPoints: Types: AVF (best, 6-8 wk maturation), graft, CVC (temporary)
Fistula care: assess thrill/bruit q shift, no BP/IV/blood draws on that arm, avoid heavy lifting, check for infection
Steal syndrome: cool pale distal hand
clinicalContext: New AVF in left forearm.
nursingPriority: Teach: feel thrill daily, no BP/IV on left arm, avoid heavy watches/tight sleeves, report pain/coolness of hand.

title: Nephrectomy
keyPoints: Indications: RCC, chronic infection, non-functional, trauma, donor
Post-op: monitor UO, other kidney function, pain, respiratory (flank incision)
DVT prophylaxis, early ambulation
clinicalContext: POD 1 right nephrectomy.
nursingPriority: Monitor UO, flank incision splinted for coughing, pain control, early ambulation, assess for bleeding.

title: Acute kidney injury
keyPoints: KDIGO: SCr rise >=0.3 in 48 h OR >=1.5x in 7 d OR UO <0.5 mL/kg/h for >6 h
Pre-renal: hypovolemia, sepsis
Intrinsic: ATN (ischemia, toxins, myoglobin), AIN
Post-renal: obstruction
Management: correct cause, avoid nephrotoxins, dialysis if AEIOU
pearls: AEIOU: Acidosis, Electrolytes (K), Ingestion, Overload, Uremia.
clinicalContext: Post-op patient with UO 15 mL/h, SCr rising.
nursingPriority: Fluid challenge 500 mL, bladder scan for obstruction, review nephrotoxic drugs, send urinalysis, consider nephrology if no response.

title: Hydronephrosis
definition: Dilation of renal pelvis/calyces due to outflow obstruction.
keyPoints: Causes: stones, BPH, tumor, stricture, pregnancy
USG diagnostic
Treatment: relieve obstruction (catheter, stent, PCN)
clinicalContext: Pregnant woman with right flank pain, USG right hydronephrosis.
nursingPriority: Physiologic in pregnancy common; if severe, urology — consider stent; monitor for infection.

title: Pyelonephritis
definition: Upper UTI — renal parenchyma + collecting system.
keyPoints: Fever, chills, flank pain, CVA tenderness, dysuria
UA: WBC casts
E coli commonest
Treatment: IV ceftriaxone or pip-tazo based on severity; stepdown to oral per culture
Repeat cultures; imaging if no response in 48-72 h
clinicalContext: Woman with fever, right flank pain, CVA tenderness, WBC casts in urine.
nursingPriority: Admit, IV ceftriaxone after cultures, IV fluids, analgesia, monitor UO, step down to oral ciprofloxacin per susceptibility.

title: Colostomy care
keyPoints: Stoma pink/red moist healthy
Output depends on level
Appliance changes q3-7 d or when leak
Skin barrier
Diet: low-residue initially, avoid gas-producing foods
clinicalContext: POD 5 left-sided colostomy.
nursingPriority: Empty pouch when 1/3 full, measure output, skin barrier, psychological support, diet counsel.

title: Acute pancreatitis
keyPoints: Diagnosis: 2/3 — typical epigastric pain, lipase >3x ULN, imaging
Etiology: gallstones (45%), alcohol (35%), hypertriglyceridemia, ERCP
Severity: Atlanta (mild, moderately severe, severe)
Management: aggressive fluids (LR), pain, NPO → early enteral nutrition if tolerated; not routine antibiotics
clinicalContext: Alcoholic with severe epigastric pain radiating to back, lipase 2500.
nursingPriority: IV lactated Ringer 5-10 mL/kg/h, analgesia, NPO initially with plan for early EN, monitor for organ failure, no prophylactic antibiotics unless infected necrosis.

title: Biliary colic
definition: RUQ pain from transient gallstone impaction at cystic duct.
keyPoints: Colicky post-fatty meal, may radiate to right shoulder
No fever/leukocytosis (vs cholecystitis)
USG shows stones
Treatment: elective lap chole
clinicalContext: Woman with post-prandial RUQ pain, USG shows stones, afebrile.
nursingPriority: Analgesia, low-fat diet, schedule elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

title: Inflammatory bowel disease (UC vs Crohn)
definition: Chronic inflammatory disorders of GI tract.
keyPoints: UC: mucosa, continuous, rectum up, bloody diarrhea, toxic megacolon, crypt abscess, PSC association
Crohn: transmural, skip lesions, any GI site, granuloma, fistula, string sign, perianal disease
Extraintestinal: arthritis, uveitis, pyoderma gangrenosum, erythema nodosum
Treatment: 5-ASA (UC), corticosteroids, immunomodulators, biologics (anti-TNF)
clinicalContext: 25-y-old with chronic bloody diarrhea, tenesmus, continuous proctocolitis on colonoscopy.
nursingPriority: Suspect UC; gastroenterology referral, start 5-ASA, steroids for flare, monitor for toxic megacolon, vaccines before biologics.

title: Ileostomy
definition: Surgical opening of small intestine to skin.
keyPoints: Output: liquid, high (1000-1500 mL/d), high Na+ loss
Skin excoriation risk — protect with barrier
Dehydration risk — >1500 mL/d high-output
Avoid high-fiber roughage
clinicalContext: New ileostomy with output 2000 mL/day.
nursingPriority: High-output — loperamide, oral rehydration with WHO ORS, IV fluid if necessary, dietary adjustments, monitor for dehydration and Na+/K+ loss.

title: Esophageal varices
definition: Dilated submucosal veins in lower esophagus from portal hypertension.
keyPoints: Risk: cirrhosis, portal vein thrombosis
Massive hematemesis, melena
Management: terlipressin/octreotide IV, endoscopic band ligation, ceftriaxone prophylaxis, TIPSS, Sengstaken-Blakemore tube temporizing
clinicalContext: Cirrhotic with large hematemesis.
nursingPriority: Two large-bore IVs, crystalloid + blood cross-match, terlipressin IV, ceftriaxone IV, urgent endoscopy for band ligation, monitor for encephalopathy.

title: Perforated duodenal ulcer
definition: Complication of peptic ulcer — gas under diaphragm on erect CXR.
keyPoints: Sudden severe epigastric pain, board-like abdomen
Peritonitis signs
Treatment: IV fluids, NG decompression, broad-spectrum antibiotics, emergency laparotomy with omental patch (Graham)
clinicalContext: Young man with sudden severe epigastric pain, rigid abdomen, CXR gas under diaphragm.
nursingPriority: NPO, NG tube, IV fluids, broad-spectrum antibiotics, urgent surgical consult for Graham patch repair, H pylori treat later.

title: Cirrhosis of liver
keyPoints: Causes: alcohol, HCV/HBV, NAFLD, autoimmune, Wilson, hemochromatosis
Complications: ascites, varices, SBP, hepatic encephalopathy, HCC, hepatorenal syndrome
Child-Pugh A/B/C; MELD score for transplant priority
clinicalContext: Cirrhotic with ascites and confusion, asterixis.
nursingPriority: Suspect hepatic encephalopathy; rule out precipitants (GI bleed, SBP, electrolyte), lactulose to 3 loose stools/day, low-protein in acute only, rifaximin, diagnostic paracentesis.

title: GERD
keyPoints: Lifestyle + PPI
Alarm symptoms → endoscopy
Nissen fundoplication for refractory
clinicalContext: Chronic GERD not responding to PPI.
nursingPriority: Optimize dose, take before meals, endoscopy for Barrett/complications, consider fundoplication.

title: Melena
definition: Black tarry stool — upper GI bleed proximal to ligament of Treitz.
keyPoints: Blood digested by gastric acid → black
Requires >50 mL blood
Causes: peptic ulcer, varices, Mallory-Weiss, cancer
Hematochezia (bright red) = lower GI or massive upper
Management: stabilize, EGD
clinicalContext: Elderly on NSAID with melena and HR 110, BP 95/60.
nursingPriority: Two large-bore IVs, crystalloid, cross-match, PPI IV pantoprazole 80 mg bolus + 8 mg/h, NPO, urgent upper endoscopy.

title: Parkinson disease
definition: Neurodegenerative disease — loss of dopaminergic nigrostriatal neurons.
keyPoints: TRAP: Tremor (resting pill-rolling), Rigidity (cogwheel), Akinesia/bradykinesia, Postural instability
Lewy bodies
Treatment: levodopa/carbidopa (gold standard), dopamine agonists (pramipexole), MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline), COMT inhibitors, DBS for advanced
clinicalContext: Elderly with resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, shuffling gait.
nursingPriority: Start levodopa/carbidopa 100/25 TDS, PT/OT, fall prevention, monitor for on-off fluctuations and dyskinesia over years.

title: Kernicterus
definition: Bilirubin encephalopathy in neonates from severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
keyPoints: Deposits in basal ganglia → athetoid cerebral palsy, hearing loss, upward gaze palsy
Prevent with phototherapy/exchange transfusion per Bhutani nomogram
Especially Rh/ABO incompatibility, G6PD deficiency
clinicalContext: Day 3 neonate with jaundice to soles, poor feeding, high-pitched cry.
nursingPriority: Intensive phototherapy, exchange transfusion if level warrants per Bhutani; also monitor hydration, treat underlying hemolysis.

title: Stroke — ischemic vs hemorrhagic
definition: Sudden focal neurological deficit from ischemia or hemorrhage.
keyPoints: Ischemic 85%: thrombotic, embolic, lacunar
Hemorrhagic 15%: ICH, SAH
FAST: Face, Arm, Speech, Time
NIHSS score
Ischemic + <4.5 h → IV alteplase 0.9 mg/kg; <24 h large-vessel → thrombectomy
BP target: ischemic <185/110 for thrombolysis; ICH <140 SBP
pearls: Time is brain — door-to-needle <60 min target.
clinicalContext: 65-y-old with sudden right arm weakness and aphasia, NIHSS 12, CT no bleed, onset 2 h ago.
nursingPriority: Within window — confirm no contraindications, IV alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (10% bolus over 1 min, rest over 60 min), BP <185/110, monitor q15 min, neuro checks.

title: Myasthenia gravis
keyPoints: Fatigable muscle weakness; ocular first (ptosis, diplopia), bulbar, respiratory
Ice test: improvement with ice
Edrophonium (Tensilon) test historic
Treatment: pyridostigmine; thymectomy; corticosteroids; IVIg/plasmapheresis for crisis
Myasthenic vs cholinergic crisis
clinicalContext: Young woman with fluctuating ptosis and difficulty chewing.
nursingPriority: Acetylcholine receptor antibody test, EMG, CT chest for thymoma, start pyridostigmine, avoid aminoglycosides/quinolones/beta-blockers that worsen.

title: Epilepsy — types and management
definition: >=2 unprovoked seizures >24 h apart or one with high recurrence risk.
keyPoints: Classification: focal, generalized (tonic-clonic, absence, myoclonic, atonic), unknown onset
First-line: levetiracetam, valproate (not in fertile women), lamotrigine
Status epilepticus: lorazepam IV → phenytoin/levetiracetam → midazolam infusion → GA
Seizure precautions: padded rails, suction, O2, lateral position
clinicalContext: Patient actively convulsing >5 min.
nursingPriority: Status epilepticus — protect airway (left lateral), O2, IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (up to 4 mg), glucose if hypoglycemic, if continues phenytoin/levetiracetam loading, ICU.

title: Guillain-Barre syndrome
keyPoints: Post-Campylobacter, CMV, Zika; ascending symmetric weakness, areflexia
CSF: albumino-cytologic dissociation (elevated protein, normal cells)
Monitor FVC — intubate if <20 mL/kg or rapid decline
Treatment: IVIg 0.4 g/kg x5 d or plasmapheresis
Avoid steroids (not effective)
clinicalContext: Ascending weakness after gastroenteritis, FVC 18 mL/kg.
nursingPriority: ICU admission, monitor bulbar and respiratory function, intubate if FVC <20 mL/kg or airway compromised, IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day x5 d.

title: Multiple sclerosis
keyPoints: Young women; relapsing-remitting most common
Symptoms: optic neuritis, Lhermitte sign, Uhthoff (heat worsens), fatigue, spasticity, bladder
MRI: periventricular white-matter plaques
Treatment: IV methylprednisolone for relapse; DMTs (interferon, glatiramer, natalizumab, ocrelizumab)
clinicalContext: Young woman with unilateral painful visual loss, prior sensory episode.
nursingPriority: MRI brain/cord, LP (oligoclonal bands), IV methylprednisolone 1 g x5 d for acute relapse, neuro referral for DMT.

title: Alzheimer dementia
keyPoints: Amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles (tau)
Progressive memory loss, language, executive decline
MMSE, MoCA screening
Treatment: cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine); memantine (NMDA) moderate-severe
Aducanumab/lecanemab novel
clinicalContext: Elderly with progressive memory loss, MoCA 18.
nursingPriority: Start donepezil 5 mg OD, caregiver support, safety assessment (driving, cooking), address reversible causes (B12, TSH, depression).

title: Meningitis
keyPoints: Bacterial: S pneumoniae, N meningitidis, H influenzae
Viral: enteroviruses — milder
Classic triad: fever, headache, neck stiffness; Kernig, Brudzinski
LP: bacterial turbid, high protein, low glucose, neutrophils
Empiric: ceftriaxone + vancomycin ± dexamethasone (pneumococcal)
clinicalContext: Adult with fever, headache, neck stiffness, photophobia.
nursingPriority: LP after ruling out raised ICP, send CSF studies, start empiric ceftriaxone 2 g BD + vancomycin within 1 h, dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg QID x4 d before or with first dose if pneumococcal suspected.

title: Brain edema — types
keyPoints: Vasogenic: BBB disruption (tumor, abscess) — responds to steroids
Cytotoxic: cellular swelling (ischemia) — no steroid benefit
Interstitial: hydrocephalus
Management: head elevation 30°, mannitol 0.25-1 g/kg, 3% hypertonic saline, hyperventilation (temporary), surgical decompression
clinicalContext: Elevated ICP >25 cm H2O in TBI.
nursingPriority: Head up 30°, mannitol 1 g/kg bolus, short hyperventilation to PaCO2 30-35, sedation, avoid hypotonic fluids, consider 3% saline, ICP monitor.

title: Tonic-clonic seizure nursing care
definition: Generalized convulsion with loss of consciousness.
keyPoints: Phases: tonic (rigid 10-20 s), clonic (jerking 1-2 min), post-ictal
Tongue biting, incontinence possible
Nursing: protect head, turn lateral, do NOT restrain or place objects in mouth, time seizure, O2 suction ready
Post-ictal: recovery position, monitor airway
clinicalContext: Ward patient begins tonic-clonic seizure.
nursingPriority: Lower to floor if standing, cushion head, left lateral position, clear surroundings, time seizure, do NOT put anything in mouth, O2 once cyanosis resolves.

title: Pontine hemorrhage
keyPoints: Sudden coma, pinpoint reactive pupils, quadriparesis, hyperthermia
Poor prognosis
Supportive care; avoid hypertension exacerbation
clinicalContext: Comatose patient with pinpoint pupils and quadriplegia after sudden headache.
nursingPriority: Airway management, neurosurgical consult, BP control, supportive; family counseling.

title: Normal respiratory rate
keyPoints: Newborn: 30-60
Infant <1 y: 30-50
Toddler 1-3 y: 24-40
Preschooler 3-6: 22-34
School-age: 18-30
Adolescent: 12-20
Adult: 12-20
clinicalContext: 2-y-old with RR 48.
nursingPriority: Tachypnea for age — assess for respiratory distress, pneumonia, fever; count for full minute.

title: Respiratory distress signs
definition: Signs of increased work of breathing.
keyPoints: Tachypnea, nasal flaring, grunting, retractions (intercostal, subcostal, suprasternal), accessory muscle use
Cyanosis
Tripoding
Silverman-Anderson score for neonates
Severe: lethargy, apneas, bradycardia → intubate
clinicalContext: Infant with tachypnea 60, intercostal retractions, grunting.
nursingPriority: Respiratory distress — O2, upright, minimal handling, consider CPAP, NBM if severe, monitor for deterioration.

title: Mantoux test
keyPoints: 0.1 mL (5 TU) PPD intradermal, inner forearm, read 48-72 h
Measure induration (not erythema)
Positive: >=5 mm (HIV, contact), >=10 mm (high-risk), >=15 mm (low-risk)
Does not distinguish active vs latent vs BCG
clinicalContext: HIV contact tested with Mantoux, induration 8 mm.
nursingPriority: Positive (HIV cutoff >=5 mm); refer for active TB workup (CXR, sputum) and IGRA if available.

title: Tuberculin test interpretation
definition: See Medicine-74 for Mantoux. Other TB tests: IGRA (QuantiFERON, T-SPOT), NAAT (CBNAAT), culture gold standard.
keyPoints: IGRA not affected by BCG
CBNAAT detects MTB + rifampicin resistance
GeneXpert in 2 h
Sputum AFB microscopy ~50% sensitivity
clinicalContext: Patient with chronic cough, CXR cavitary upper zone.
nursingPriority: Send sputum for CBNAAT (detects MTB + rifampicin resistance in 2 h), register under NTEP if positive, start 4-drug regimen.

title: Pulmonary edema
keyPoints: Cardiogenic: high PCWP, LVF, MI, MR
Non-cardiogenic: ARDS (normal PCWP)
Symptoms: orthopnea, PND, pink frothy sputum, bilateral crackles
Treatment: LMNOP — Lasix, Morphine, Nitrates, Oxygen, Position (upright)
clinicalContext: Acute pulmonary edema patient.
nursingPriority: Sit upright with legs dependent, high-flow O2, furosemide 40 mg IV, nitroglycerin drip, BiPAP if respiratory fatigue, monitor vitals and UO.

title: Obstructive sleep apnea
definition: Upper airway collapse in sleep — AHI >=5.
keyPoints: Loud snoring, witnessed apneas, daytime sleepiness, morning headache
STOP-BANG screening
Polysomnography diagnostic
Treatment: CPAP first-line, weight loss, oral appliance, UPPP surgery
Consequences: HTN, AF, MI, stroke
clinicalContext: Obese man with loud snoring and daytime sleepiness.
nursingPriority: Refer for polysomnography; if AHI >=5 and symptomatic, start CPAP, weight loss, counsel driving risk.

title: PEEP — indications and contraindications
keyPoints: Indications: ARDS, atelectasis, recruit alveoli, improve oxygenation
Typical 5-15 cm H2O; higher in ARDS per PEEP table
Complications: barotrauma, reduced venous return, reduced CO, raised ICP
Contraindication: tension pneumothorax untreated, severe right heart failure
clinicalContext: ARDS patient with PaO2/FiO2 80 on PEEP 5.
nursingPriority: Increase PEEP per table (likely 10-15 based on FiO2), monitor plateau <30, lung-protective Vt 6 mL/kg, prone if P/F <150.

title: Lung cancer
keyPoints: Small-cell (15%, smoking, paraneoplastic SIADH/Cushing) vs Non-small-cell (85%)
NSCLC: adenocarcinoma (commonest, non-smokers), squamous (central, PTHrP hypercalcemia), large-cell
Risk: smoking (#1), asbestos, radon, second-hand smoke
Screening: low-dose CT in high-risk >=50 y smokers
Treatment: surgery (early NSCLC), chemo, radio, targeted (EGFR, ALK), immunotherapy
clinicalContext: 55-y-old smoker with new cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, CT mass.
nursingPriority: Biopsy for histology and molecular testing, staging PET-CT, pulmonary function, multidisciplinary oncology review, smoking cessation support.

title: Pulmonary embolism
definition: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries by thromboembolus.
keyPoints: Risk: Virchow triad (stasis, endothelial injury, hypercoagulability)
Symptoms: sudden dyspnea, chest pain, tachycardia, hypoxia
Wells score; D-dimer sensitive (rule-out); CTPA gold standard
Treatment: anticoagulation (LMWH/DOAC); thrombolysis if massive PE; IVC filter if anticoag contraindicated
clinicalContext: Post-op hip surgery with sudden dyspnea, SpO2 88%, tachycardia.
nursingPriority: O2, CTPA, start LMWH (enoxaparin 1 mg/kg BD) pending result, elevate head, telemetry, prepare for thrombolysis if massive.

topic: Occupational lung disease — bagassosis, Monday fever/byssinosis
title: Occupational lung disease — bagassosis, Monday fever/byssinosis
keyPoints: Silicosis: sandblasting, mining — eggshell calcification; TB risk
Asbestosis: shipbuilding — pleural plaques, mesothelioma
Coal workers pneumoconiosis (black lung)
Bagassosis: sugarcane (thermophilic actinomycetes)
Byssinosis (Monday fever): cotton mill
Farmer lung: moldy hay
clinicalContext: Cotton-mill worker with Monday morning dyspnea.
nursingPriority: Byssinosis — remove from exposure, bronchodilators, vaccinate, counsel ESI benefits, spirometry monitoring.

title: Apnea
keyPoints: Newborn apnea: >20 s or <20 s with bradycardia/cyanosis/hypotonia
Central: no effort; obstructive: effort without airflow; mixed
Treatment newborn: tactile stimulation, CPAP, caffeine citrate
clinicalContext: Preterm 32-wk with recurrent apneas.
nursingPriority: Apnea of prematurity — start caffeine citrate 20 mg/kg loading then 5-10 mg/kg/day, CPAP, monitor, positioning prone or side-lying.

title: Pulmonary function test
keyPoints: FEV1: forced expiratory volume in 1 s
FVC: forced vital capacity
FEV1/FVC ratio: normal >=0.7; <0.7 = obstructive (asthma, COPD)
Restrictive: FEV1/FVC normal but both reduced (fibrosis, obesity)
Reversibility >12% and 200 mL = asthma
clinicalContext: Smoker with FEV1/FVC 0.55, FEV1 55% predicted.
nursingPriority: COPD GOLD 2 moderate; bronchodilators, smoking cessation, pulmonary rehab, vaccines, check ABG if severe.

title: Cheyne-Stokes respiration
definition: Periodic breathing pattern: crescendo-decrescendo with apnea.
keyPoints: Causes: CHF, stroke, uremia, high altitude, opioids
Due to delayed chemoreceptor feedback
Kussmaul = deep rapid (DKA), Biot = irregular (brainstem)
clinicalContext: Elderly CHF patient with crescendo-decrescendo breathing pattern.
nursingPriority: Document Cheyne-Stokes, optimize CHF treatment, consider sleep study, monitor overnight SpO2.

topic: Cessation of breathing — brain death criteria
title: Cessation of breathing — brain death criteria
definition: Irreversible cessation of all brain including brainstem function.
keyPoints: Criteria: coma, absent brainstem reflexes (pupil, corneal, oculocephalic, oculovestibular, gag, cough), apnea test positive
Repeat exam after interval
Exclude confounders: hypothermia, drugs, severe metabolic
Legal requirement for organ donation
clinicalContext: Ventilated patient 72 h post severe TBI with fixed pupils.
nursingPriority: Exclude drugs/hypothermia, perform brainstem reflex exam by 2 physicians, apnea test, document per institutional protocol, discuss organ donation with family.

title: Pneumonia
keyPoints: CAP: S pneumoniae commonest; atypical (Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, Legionella)
HAP: >48 h after admission; Pseudomonas, MRSA
CURB-65: Confusion, Urea >7, RR >=30, BP <90/60, age >=65
Treatment CAP: amoxicillin ± macrolide; HAP: broad-spectrum per local antibiogram
clinicalContext: 65-y-old with fever, cough, RR 32, BP 85/55, BUN 9.
nursingPriority: CURB-65 score 4 — admit ICU, blood cultures, IV ceftriaxone + azithromycin, O2, fluids, HAP coverage if hospitalized >48 h.

title: Scrotum — conditions
keyPoints: Hydrocele: transilluminates
Varicocele: bag of worms, left > right
Epididymitis: tender epididymis + fever
Torsion: sudden pain, elevated testis, absent cremasteric
Testicular tumor: painless mass
clinicalContext: Young adult with painless right testicular mass, no transillumination.
nursingPriority: Testicular cancer until proven otherwise — do NOT biopsy transscrotally; order USG, tumor markers (AFP, β-hCG, LDH), refer urology.

title: Exstrophy of bladder
definition: See Surgery-27. Congenital anterior abdominal wall and bladder failure.
keyPoints: Cover bladder with plastic wrap at birth
Urinary reconstruction staged
Avoid latex
clinicalContext: Newborn bladder exstrophy.
nursingPriority: Cover with plastic wrap, no gauze, pediatric urology urgent referral.

title: Urolithiasis
keyPoints: Types: Ca oxalate (80%), struvite (infection — staghorn), uric acid (radiolucent), cystine
NCCT KUB gold standard
Treatment: <5 mm often pass; 5-10 mm MET with tamsulosin; >10 mm SWL/ureteroscopy; staghorn PCNL
clinicalContext: Patient with colicky flank pain, stone 8 mm in distal ureter.
nursingPriority: Analgesia (diclofenac IM), hydration, tamsulosin 0.4 mg OD (MET), strain urine; urology follow-up; imaging reassessment.

title: Urinary incontinence — types
keyPoints: Stress: leak with cough/laugh (weak pelvic floor); Kegel, pessary
Urge (overactive bladder): sudden urgency; anticholinergic (oxybutynin), β3-agonist (mirabegron)
Overflow: retention with dribbling; BPH, DM neuropathy
Functional: mobility/cognition; toilet routine
Mixed
clinicalContext: Post-partum woman with leakage on coughing.
nursingPriority: Stress incontinence — Kegel pelvic floor exercises 3 sets of 10 BD, weight management, biofeedback; refer for pessary/surgery if severe.

title: Fecal incontinence
keyPoints: Causes: obstetric injury, neurologic (MS, cauda equina), diarrhea, impaction with overflow
Evaluation: endoanal USG, manometry
Treatment: dietary fiber, bulk-forming, biofeedback, sphincteroplasty
clinicalContext: Elderly with fecal soiling and chronic constipation.
nursingPriority: Rule out fecal impaction with overflow — disimpact, start bulk-forming laxative and scheduled toileting, refer for evaluation.

title: HIV — stages and management
keyPoints: Stages: acute (seroconversion) → clinical latency → AIDS (CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness)
Screening: ELISA → Western blot / rapid tests; viral load monitor
ART: start all regardless of CD4 (NACP V); first-line TLD (TDF + 3TC + DTG)
Opportunistic: PCP (<200), MAC (<50), CMV, toxoplasmosis
clinicalContext: New HIV diagnosis with CD4 180.
nursingPriority: Start TLD (TDF 300 + 3TC 300 + DTG 50) daily, PCP prophylaxis with cotrimoxazole DS OD, screen TB, counsel adherence, partner testing.

title: Kaposi sarcoma
keyPoints: Classic, endemic (African), immunosuppression (transplant), AIDS-associated
Violaceous plaques/nodules on skin and mucosa; may involve GI, lung
Treatment: ART (often regresses with immune reconstitution), local therapy, systemic chemo for visceral
clinicalContext: AIDS patient with purple plaques on palate and legs.
nursingPriority: Classic KS — start/optimize ART, refer to oncology for systemic involvement.

title: Wasting syndrome
definition: AIDS-defining involuntary loss >10% body weight + chronic diarrhea/fatigue/fever >30 d.
keyPoints: Multifactorial: OI, malabsorption, anorexia
Treat cause, nutritional support, ART
Appetite stimulants, resistance training
clinicalContext: Advanced HIV with 15% weight loss and chronic diarrhea.
nursingPriority: Evaluate for OI, start ART if not on, nutritional consult, enteral supplement, treat underlying diarrhea etiology.

title: Urinary tract infection (UTI)
definition: Lower or upper urinary tract infection.
keyPoints: Women commoner; E coli 80%
Uncomplicated lower UTI: nitrofurantoin 5 d, fosfomycin 3 g single dose, cefuroxime, cotrimoxazole
Complicated/pyelonephritis: ciprofloxacin or IV ceftriaxone
Recurrent: post-coital prophylaxis, topical estrogen (menopause)
clinicalContext: Non-pregnant woman with dysuria, frequency, nitrite +.
nursingPriority: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BD x5 d; hydration; follow-up if symptoms persist.

title: Healthcare-associated infections (HAI)
keyPoints: CLABSI: central line >48 h — bundles (CHG bath, hand hygiene, max barrier)
CAUTI: Foley >48 h — remove ASAP, closed drainage
VAP: ventilator >48 h — HOB 30°, oral CHG, SAT/SBT
SSI: see Surgery
C difficile: soap and water (not alcohol), contact precautions
clinicalContext: ICU with rising CLABSI rate.
nursingPriority: Implement central line bundle — hand hygiene, maximum sterile barrier, CHG skin prep, optimal site (subclavian > IJ > femoral), daily review of need.

topic: Skin lesions — wheal, vesicle, papule, macule
title: Skin lesions — wheal, vesicle, papule, macule
keyPoints: Macule: flat, <=1 cm (freckle)
Papule: raised <=1 cm (wart)
Plaque: flat-topped >1 cm (psoriasis)
Nodule: raised >1 cm
Vesicle: fluid-filled <=1 cm (chickenpox)
Bulla: >1 cm (burn blister)
Pustule: pus-filled
Wheal: transient raised (urticaria)
clinicalContext: Itchy raised transient lesion on arm 30 min after shellfish.
nursingPriority: Wheals in urticaria — stop allergen, antihistamine cetirizine 10 mg, watch for anaphylaxis (wheeze, hypotension, airway swelling).

title: Contact dermatitis
definition: Type IV hypersensitivity or irritant reaction.
keyPoints: Allergic: nickel, poison ivy
Irritant: detergents, acids
Treatment: identify and remove trigger, topical steroids, antihistamines
Patch testing for allergen identification
clinicalContext: Nurse with erythematous itchy hands after latex glove use.
nursingPriority: Suspect latex allergy — switch to nitrile gloves, topical hydrocortisone, oral antihistamine, patch test to confirm, document.

title: Scabies
keyPoints: Intense itching especially night, interdigital web burrows, genital nodules
Treatment: permethrin 5% cream, head to toe, wash off after 8-12 h, repeat in 7 d; ivermectin 200 mcg/kg PO alternative
Treat all household contacts, wash linen hot water
clinicalContext: Family with intense nocturnal itch and web-space burrows.
nursingPriority: Permethrin 5% to all household members simultaneously, wash linen >60°C or bag 72 h, repeat in 1 wk.

title: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS)
definition: Stevens-Johnson syndrome — severe mucocutaneous drug reaction.
keyPoints: <10% BSA detachment = SJS; 10-30% = SJS/TEN overlap; >30% = TEN
Common drugs: carbamazepine, allopurinol, sulfonamides, lamotrigine
Nikolsky sign positive
Management: stop offending drug, burn-unit-like care, fluids, pain, monitor eyes, IVIg/cyclosporine
clinicalContext: Patient on allopurinol develops rash + mucous membrane involvement + 15% BSA.
nursingPriority: Stop allopurinol immediately, transfer to burn/ICU unit, fluid + electrolyte, wound care, ophthalmology for eye involvement, report ADR.

title: Barium enema
definition: Fluoroscopic study of colon with barium contrast.
keyPoints: Indications: suspected obstruction, volvulus, Hirschsprung, intussusception (also therapeutic)
Prep: bowel prep, NPO overnight
Post-procedure: laxative to clear barium, hydrate
Contraindicated: suspected perforation (use gastrografin)
clinicalContext: Suspected intussusception in infant.
nursingPriority: Diagnostic + therapeutic air or barium enema under fluoroscopy; contraindicated if perforation; surgical standby.

title: X-ray interpretation basics
keyPoints: Tension pneumothorax: mediastinal shift, flat diaphragm, no lung markings
CHF: cardiomegaly, Kerley B lines, bat-wing
Pneumonia: consolidation with air bronchograms
TB: upper zone cavitation, miliary reticulonodular
Hyaline membrane: ground glass + air bronchograms in preterm
clinicalContext: Preterm neonate CXR shows reticulogranular pattern with air bronchograms.
nursingPriority: RDS (hyaline membrane disease) — surfactant via ETT, CPAP/ventilation, thermoregulation.

title: Hypertensive emergency vs urgency
definition: Emergency = severe HTN + target-organ damage. Urgency = severe HTN without organ damage.
keyPoints: Emergency: stroke, MI, aortic dissection, PE, eclampsia, encephalopathy, retinal hemorrhage
Treatment: IV labetalol, nicardipine, sodium nitroprusside; goal reduce MAP 10-25% in first hour
Aortic dissection: SBP <120 rapidly + HR <60
Ischemic stroke: don't lower BP unless >220/120 or thrombolysis
clinicalContext: BP 220/130 with new chest pain and dyspnea.
nursingPriority: Hypertensive emergency — ICU admission, IV nitroglycerin + beta-blocker, target MAP reduction 10-25% in 1 h, monitor end-organs.

title: Heart failure — classification and nursing
keyPoints: HFrEF (EF <=40): ischemic, DCM
HFpEF (EF >=50): elderly HTN, diabetes
NYHA I-IV functional class
BNP elevated
Treatment HFrEF: ACE-i/ARNI + beta-blocker + MRA + SGLT2i; diuretic for symptoms
Device: ICD, CRT
Salt <2 g/d, fluid <2 L/d
clinicalContext: HFrEF patient with dyspnea, pitting edema, weight gain 3 kg in 3 d.
nursingPriority: Daily weights, sodium <2 g, fluid <2 L, optimize ACE-i/sacubitril-valsartan + beta-blocker + MRA + empagliflozin, furosemide PRN.

title: COPD — emphysema vs chronic bronchitis
keyPoints: Emphysema: destruction of alveolar walls, "pink puffers"
Chronic bronchitis: productive cough >3 mo x2 y, "blue bloaters"
GOLD ABE grouping, FEV1 based staging
Treatment: bronchodilators (LABA/LAMA), inhaled steroid in frequent exacerbators, pulmonary rehab, vaccines, O2 if PaO2 <55
Smoking cessation most impactful
clinicalContext: COPD exacerbation with increased dyspnea and sputum.
nursingPriority: Nebulized salbutamol + ipratropium, oral prednisolone 40 mg x5 d, antibiotic if purulent sputum, controlled O2 SpO2 88-92%, assess need for NIV.

title: Asthma — nursing management adult
definition: Chronic airway inflammation with reversible obstruction.
keyPoints: Symptoms: wheeze, cough, dyspnea, chest tightness especially night/early morning
Spirometry reversibility
GINA stepwise: ICS-LABA even in mild
Acute: SABA nebulizer, oxygen SpO2 94-98%, oral steroid, consider MgSO4
Status asthmaticus: ICU, consider intubation
clinicalContext: Adult with severe acute asthma, PEFR 40% predicted, unable to speak sentences.
nursingPriority: O2 high-flow, salbutamol + ipratropium nebulization back-to-back, IV hydrocortisone 100 mg, magnesium sulfate 2 g IV if no response, monitor for intubation.

title: Acute coronary syndrome — MONA
definition: Initial therapy for acute coronary syndrome: MONA-B.
keyPoints: Morphine, Oxygen (if SpO2 <90%), Nitroglycerin, Aspirin 325 mg chewed
Plus Beta-blocker if no contraindication, statin high-intensity, heparin
Avoid nitrates in inferior MI with RV involvement, severe AS, sildenafil <24 h
Door-to-balloon <90 min for STEMI
clinicalContext: Chest pain patient, STEMI anterior.
nursingPriority: ASA 325 chew, ticagrelor 180 mg loading, heparin bolus, morphine PRN, nitroglycerin SL, O2 if hypoxic, call cath lab, prep for PCI.

title: Cardiogenic shock
definition: Cardiac output inadequate for tissue perfusion despite euvolemia.
keyPoints: MI commonest cause
Hypotension, elevated filling pressures, low CI
Treatment: inotropes (dobutamine, milrinone), pressors (norepinephrine), revascularization, IABP/Impella/ECMO, avoid excess fluids
clinicalContext: Post-MI BP 80/50, cool extremities, oliguria, crackles.
nursingPriority: ICU, norepinephrine + dobutamine titrate MAP >=65, urgent PCI for underlying MI, consider IABP, strict I/O, avoid excess fluid.

title: Peripheral arterial disease
keyPoints: Intermittent claudication, rest pain, ulcers, 6 Ps in acute (pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia)
ABI <=0.9 diagnostic; <0.4 severe
Risk factors: smoking, DM, HTN
Management: smoking cessation, statin, antiplatelet, exercise therapy; cilostazol; revascularization
clinicalContext: Diabetic smoker with calf cramping at 100 m walking.
nursingPriority: ABI, address risk factors, start aspirin + statin, supervised exercise program, smoking cessation; refer if lifestyle-limiting.

title: Liver function tests
keyPoints: AST/ALT: hepatocellular injury; AST:ALT >2 alcohol; >1000 ischemic/viral/toxic
ALP: cholestasis, bone
GGT: confirms hepatic ALP
Bilirubin: direct vs indirect
Albumin, PT/INR: synthetic function
LDH: hemolysis, liver
clinicalContext: Patient with jaundice, AST 1800, ALT 2000, INR 1.8.
nursingPriority: Acute hepatitis — check viral serology, paracetamol level, autoimmune, alcohol; supportive care, monitor coagulation and encephalopathy; urgent hepatology.
